Methods A mixed‐methods approach was employed, combining latent profile analysis (LPA) and epistemic network analysis (ENA). Objectives This study explores students' perceptions of how well their institutions prepare them for AI‐related workplace challenges, how relevant they perceive their AI education to be to industry expectations, and which learning experiences they see as most useful for developing valued AI competencies. title: Mapping Research on Generative Artificial Intelligence for Programming Education: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Mapping Research on Generative Artificial Intelligence for Programming Education: A Systematic Review ABSTRACT Background Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to transform programming education, yet existing research on its integration and impact remains fragmented, underscoring the need for a comprehensive synthesis. Objectives This systematic review aims to consolidate empirical evidence on the use of generative AI in programming education within higher education, examining research objectives, AI tools, instructional strategies, programming languages and publication trends. Methods Following PRISMA guidelines, 46 peer‐reviewed empirical studies were analysed to identify patterns in tool usage, pedagogical approaches and research dissemination. Results and Conclusion ChatGPT dominated the literature, featuring in 76% of studies, while Java and Python were the most frequently targeted programming languages. title: Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality Technology for Safety Training in High‐Risk Environments: A Systematic Literature Review on Perspectives and Challenges
text_snippet: Virtual Reality and Augmented Reality Technology for Safety Training in High‐Risk Environments: A Systematic Literature Review on Perspectives and Challenges ABSTRACT Background Effective safety training in high‐risk industries including construction, mining, manufacturing, aviation and nuclear energy is critically important, as inadequate hazard awareness and human error consistently contribute to occupational fatalities and severe incidents. Method This systematic review synthesises evidence from 66 studies published between 2015 and 2026 across 29 countries to evaluate the application and effectiveness of virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR) technologies for safety training in these sectors. While prior studies recognize the value of emotion analysis and feedback, they typically rely on static or snapshot measures, limiting insights into the temporal evolution of learners' affective states and constraining timely interventions. Objectives This study aims to develop a time‐series sentiment analysis model that enables real‐time, automated monitoring and feedback of teachers' emotional states in online learning environments, thereby enhancing engagement, self‐regulation, and overall learning effectiveness. text_snippet: Collaborative Learning: A Transactional Approach to Examining Collaborative Processes and Outcomes ABSTRACT Background Research on collaborative learning has long examined processes and outcomes separately, with distinct fields—Computer‐Supported Collaborative Learning (CSCL), learning sciences and recently learning analytics—drawing on differing epistemological premises. text_snippet: The Impact of ChatGPT on Higher Education: A Systematic Review of Global Opportunities, Perceptions, and Challenges ABSTRACT Background The advent of artificial intelligence (AI) has fundamentally changed how education is delivered and how students perform. title: Do Digital Textbooks Boost Students' Learning Motivation? Evidence From a Meta‐Analysis
text_snippet: Do Digital Textbooks Boost Students' Learning Motivation? Evidence From a Meta‐Analysis ABSTRACT Background Compared to paper textbooks, digital textbooks (DTs) offer greater accessibility, multimodal representations, and interactivity, which might boost personalized and social learning and greater motivation. However, past DT studies showed mixed results: more learning versus non‐significant results versus less learning. Objectives Hence, this meta‐analysis (a) determines the overall effect of DTs (vs. paper textbooks) on student motivation, and (b) identifies moderators that account for different effect sizes across the original studies. Methods We conducted a random‐effects meta‐analysis of 42 effect sizes from 27 experimental/quasi‐experimental studies of 3590 participants. Results and Conclusions Compared to paper textbooks, DTs boosted students' intrinsic motivation ( g = 0.536) but not their extrinsic motivation. DT effects were larger for (a) collectivist cultures than individualist cultures; and (b) students at higher educational levels. Implications Educators and policymakers can consider how to help students use DTs to improve their motivation, especially starting with intrinsic motivation in collectivist cultures among older students.
